title: Fabric Governance from Tenant to Item
purpose: Show how governance authority narrows from tenant defaults through delegated domains and workspaces to item and data controls.
accessibleSummary: Four nested scopes: tenant administrators establish defaults and delegation, domain administrators govern business groupings, workspace roles control collaboration, and item or data controls protect individual assets.
longDescription: The diagram reads from tenant to domain, workspace, and item. Tenant settings establish organization-wide defaults and delegate selected controls. Domains group Fabric content by business area. Workspaces provide collaboration and capacity boundaries. Item permissions, labels, endorsement, and supported row, column, or table controls protect the final asset.

nodes.label: Tenant governance
nodes.summary: Fabric administrators establish defaults, audit policy, and delegated settings.
nodes.detail: Fabric administrators establish defaults, audit policy, and delegated settings. Configure tenant settings, auditing, protection defaults, and delegation.
nodes.whyItMatters: An enterprise baseline plus explicitly delegated controls depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Fabric governance uses tenant defaults with delegated domain overrides and granular workspace controls.

inputs: Enterprise risk policy and regulatory obligations
processing: Configure tenant settings, auditing, protection defaults, and delegation
outputs: An enterprise baseline plus explicitly delegated controls
drill.example: An administrator enables sensitivity-label policy tenant-wide and delegates a domain discovery setting.
controls: Tenant administrator roles and change review
failureModes: Over-broad delegation lets domains weaken an enterprise baseline

nodes.label: Business domains
nodes.summary: Domains group workspaces and apply governance delegated for a business area.
nodes.detail: Domains group workspaces and apply governance delegated for a business area. Assign ownership, group workspaces, and apply permitted overrides.
nodes.whyItMatters: A discoverable business-area boundary in the OneLake catalog depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Domains group content by business area, can contain subdomains, and apply delegated settings.

processing: Assign ownership, group workspaces, and apply permitted overrides
outputs: A discoverable business-area boundary in the OneLake catalog
drill.example: Finance groups planning and actuals workspaces and applies its endorsement policy.
failureModes: Treating a domain grouping as proof of data-level isolation

nodes.label: Workspace boundary
nodes.summary: Workspace owners apply the most granular workspace-scoped governance controls.
nodes.detail: Workspace owners apply the most granular workspace-scoped governance controls. Place governed items together and configure the controls available at this scope.
nodes.whyItMatters: A collaboration boundary with named owners depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Fabric's governance hierarchy narrows from tenant defaults and domain overrides to controls managed at workspace scope.

inputs: Domain membership, capacity assignment, and team identities
processing: Place governed items together and configure workspace-scoped controls
outputs: A collaboration boundary with named owners
drill.example: A reporting workspace keeps certified consumption items separate from engineering work in another workspace.
controls: Entra groups, roles, and capacity assignment
failureModes: Using a single broad workspace for unrelated teams obscures ownership and control boundaries

nodes.label: Item and data controls
nodes.summary: Permissions, labels, endorsement, and supported granular security protect the asset.
nodes.detail: Permissions, labels, endorsement, and supported granular security protect the asset. Apply item permission, label, endorsement, and path-specific data security.
nodes.whyItMatters: A discoverable asset with enforced access depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Fabric supports sensitivity labels, endorsement, item discovery, and granular controls on specified serving surfaces.

inputs: A governed item and its consumer personas
processing: Apply item permission, label, endorsement, and path-specific data security
outputs: A discoverable asset with enforced access
drill.example: A certified sales model carries a sensitivity label and regional row filtering.
controls: Sharing, label, endorsement, and RLS or OLS
failureModes: Assuming SQL endpoint rules also secure Spark or file access

edges.label: contains and grants access to items
